input.strategy_title: Adopt structured JSON logging across RHOAI components
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

RHOAI components log in inconsistent formats — plain text, key=value, and
ad-hoc JSON — which breaks centralized log queries and makes support cases
expensive: correlating one user request across Dashboard, serving, and
pipelines requires per-component parsing rules. The platform needs one
structured logging convention, and each component needs to adopt it. Component
adoptions are independent of each other once the convention exists.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1  | P0 | A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema, required fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id), and library guidance per language (Go, Python, TypeScript). |
| HLR-2  | P0 | Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-3  | P0 | KServe controller and serving runtimes emit convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-4  | P1 | Data Science Pipelines (operator and API server) emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-5  | P1 | Model Registry emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-6  | P1 | TrustyAI services emit convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-7  | P1 | Notebooks (notebook-controller) emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-8  | P2 | Training Operator emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-9  | P2 | Documentation describes the log format and example queries for common support scenarios. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- KServe
- Data Science Pipelines
- Model Registry
- TrustyAI
- Notebooks
- Training Operator

## Out of Scope

- Log storage, retention, or forwarding infrastructure
- Metrics and tracing conventions (logging only)

## Open Questions

None — the convention work (HLR-1) is prerequisite design, and per-component
adoptions are mechanical once it lands.

# Publish RHOAI structured JSON logging convention

## Description

This epic delivers the platform structured logging convention that all RHOAI
component adoptions build against: a published specification of the JSON log
schema, the required fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace,
correlation id), and library guidance for each supported language (Go, Python,
TypeScript). It is the prerequisite design work for every per-component
adoption in this strategy.

## Scope

- Define the JSON log schema: field names, types, and semantics for the
  required fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id),
  plus rules for optional/extension fields.
- Specify conformance rules: what makes a log line "convention-conformant"
  (valid JSON, required fields present and correctly typed), so each adopting
  component has an unambiguous pass/fail target.
- Provide library guidance per language: recommended logging libraries and
  configuration approaches for Go, Python, and TypeScript services, including
  how the correlation id is carried and emitted.
- Include worked example log lines that validate against the schema.
- Publish the convention in the platform documentation/standards location so
  component teams can reference it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published convention defines a JSON schema in which every required field
  (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id) has a specified name
  and type.
- The convention includes library guidance for Go, Python, and TypeScript.
- Every example log line in the convention validates against the published
  schema (automated validation, pass/fail).
- The convention has been reviewed and acknowledged by the owning teams of all
  adopting components (Dashboard, serving, pipelines, Model Registry, TrustyAI,
  notebooks, Training Operator) before adoptions begin.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema,
  required fields, and library guidance per language.

# Adopt convention-conformant structured logging in Dashboard

## Description

This epic converts the RHOAI Dashboard (the single-pane web console) to emit
structured JSON logs that conform to the published platform logging
convention, so Dashboard activity can be correlated with serving and pipeline
activity in centralized log queries.

## Scope

- Replace ad-hoc Dashboard log output (plain text / key=value / unstructured
  JSON) with convention-conformant JSON log records carrying the required
  fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id).
- Apply the convention's TypeScript library guidance to the Dashboard's
  logging setup.
- Propagate or emit a correlation id for user-initiated Dashboard requests so
  a single user action can be traced across the platform per the strategy's
  problem statement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Log output from the Dashboard is valid JSON conforming to the published
  convention schema, with all required fields present and correctly typed
  (verified by schema validation over captured sample logs, pass/fail).
- Log records for a user-initiated Dashboard request carry a correlation id
  usable for cross-component correlation.
- Existing consumers of Dashboard logs (dashboards, alerts, support tooling)
  are identified and verified to tolerate the new format, or a documented
  fallback is provided for any that do not.
- The Dashboard build pipeline is green with the logging changes merged.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs.

# Adopt convention-conformant structured logging in serving runtimes

## Description

This epic converts the model-serving runtimes used for model execution
(vLLM, OpenVINO, Caikit) to emit structured JSON logs conforming to the
published platform logging convention, so inference-serving activity can be
correlated with Dashboard and pipeline activity.

## Scope

- Bring the log output of each serving runtime image shipped by the platform
  into conformance with the convention: valid JSON records with the required
  fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id).
- Apply the convention's per-language library guidance (Python for vLLM and
  Caikit; the applicable guidance for OpenVINO-based runtimes).
- Decide and document, per runtime, whether conformance is achieved via
  upstream contributions or midstream patches, keeping carried patches
  minimal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Log output from each platform-shipped serving runtime is valid JSON
  conforming to the published convention schema, with all required fields
  present and correctly typed (verified by schema validation over captured
  sample logs, pass/fail).
- The upstream-vs-midstream approach is documented for each runtime, and any
  midstream patches are recorded.
- Existing consumers of runtime logs (dashboards, alerts, support tooling)
  are identified and verified to tolerate the new format, or a documented
  fallback is provided for any that do not.
- The build pipeline for each modified runtime image is green with the
  logging changes merged.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): KServe controller and serving runtimes emit convention-
  conformant logs (serving-runtimes portion).

## Risks / Notes

- The runtimes are upstream-venored projects; conformant logging may require
  upstream contributions or carried midstream patches, which adds coordination
  risk relative to the other adoptions.
